ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, point $P$ is the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of $AB$ and $BC$, and point $Q$ is symmetric to point $P$ with respect to $AC$. Connect $PC$, $PQ$, and $CQ$. If in $\triangle PCQ$ there is an angle of $50^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect AP and BP as shown in the diagram: \\
$\because$ Point P is the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC,\\
$\therefore$ PA = PB = PC,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$PAB = $\angle$PBA, $\angle$PBC = $\angle$PCB, $\angle$PAC = $\angle$PCA,\\
$\because$ Point Q is symmetric to point P with respect to AC,\\
$\therefore$ PC = QC, $\angle$PCA = $\angle$QCA,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$CPQ = $\angle$CQP,\\
(1) When $\angle$CPQ = $\angle$CQP = 50$^\circ$, $\angle$PCQ = 80$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$PCA = 40$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$PAC = 40$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$PAB + $\angle$PBA + $\angle$PBC + $\angle$PCB = 180$^\circ$ - $\angle$PAC - $\angle$PCA = 100$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ 2$\angle$ABP + 2$\angle$PBC = 100$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ABP + $\angle$PBC = 50$^\circ$, i.e., $\angle$ABC = 50$^\circ$,\\
(2) When $\angle$PCQ = 50$^\circ$, $\angle$PCA = 25$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$PAC = 25$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$PAB + $\angle$PBA + $\angle$PBC + $\angle$PCB = 180$^\circ$ - $\angle$PAC - $\angle$PCA = 130$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ 2$\angle$ABP + 2$\angle$PBC = 130$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ABP + $\angle$PBC = 65$^\circ$, i.e., $\angle$ABC = 65$^\circ$,\\
In conclusion, $\angle$ABC is \boxed{50^\circ} or \boxed{65^\circ}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows triangle ABC with B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and A at the top. Segments AB, BC, and AC form the main triangle. Point P is drawn inside/right of the main triangle near C. Point Q is drawn to the right of AC and above C, on the opposite side of AC from P. The segments PC, PQ, and CQ are drawn, forming triangle PCQ, and PQ crosses the line AC. Reasoning: Add auxiliary segments AP and BP. Since P is the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC, P is equidistant from A, B, and C, so PA = PB = PC. Hence triangle PAB is isosceles, giving ∠PAB = ∠PBA; triangle PBC is isosceles, giving ∠PBC = ∠PCB; and PA = PC gives ∠PAC = ∠PCA. Since Q is the reflection of P across AC, C lies on the mirror axis AC, so PC = QC, and AC bisects ∠PCQ; thus ∠PCA = ∠QCA. Therefore triangle PCQ is isosceles with base angles ∠CPQ = ∠CQP. Let θ = ∠PCA = ∠PAC. Then ∠PCQ = 2θ. There are two possible positions for the given 50° angle in triangle PCQ. Case 1: If the 50° angle is a base angle, then ∠CPQ = ∠CQP = 50°, so ∠PCQ = 180° - 50° - 50° = 80°. Thus 2θ = 80°, so θ = 40°. In triangle ABC, write ∠B = ∠ABP + ∠PBC. Let ∠ABP = ∠PAB = x and ∠PBC = ∠PCB = y. Then the angles of triangle ABC are x + θ, x + y, and y + θ, so 2x + 2y + 2θ = 180°. Therefore x + y = 90° - θ. Hence ∠B = 90° - 40° = 50°. Case 2: If the 50° angle is the vertex angle ∠PCQ, then 2θ = 50°, so θ = 25°. Again ∠B = 90° - θ = 90° - 25° = 65°. Therefore the possible measures of ∠B are 50° or 65°.

The segments PC, PQ, and CQ are drawn, forming triangle PCQ, and PQ crosses the line AC. Reasoning: Add auxiliary segments AP and BP. Since P is the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC, P is equidistant from A, B, and C, so PA = PB = PC. Hence triangle PAB is isosceles, giving ∠PAB = ∠PBA; triangle PBC is isosceles, giving ∠PBC = ∠PCB; and PA = PC gives ∠PAC = ∠PCA. Since Q is the reflection of P across AC, C lies on the mirror axis AC, so PC = QC, and AC bisects ∠PCQ; thus ∠PCA = ∠QCA. Therefore triangle PCQ is isosceles with base angles ∠CPQ = ∠CQP. Let θ = ∠PCA = ∠PAC. Then ∠PCQ = 2θ. There are two possible positions for the given 50° angle in triangle PCQ. Case 1: If the 50° angle is a base angle, then ∠CPQ = ∠CQP = 50°, so ∠PCQ = 180° - 50° - 50° = 80°. Thus 2θ = 80°, so θ = 40°. In triangle ABC, write ∠B = ∠ABP + ∠PBC. Let ∠ABP = ∠PAB = x and ∠PBC = ∠PCB = y. Then the angles of triangle ABC are x + θ, x + y, and y + θ, so 2x + 2y + 2θ = 180°. Therefore x + y = 90° - θ. Hence ∠B = 90° - 40° = 50°. Case 2: If the 50° angle is the vertex angle ∠PCQ, then 2θ = 50°, so θ = 25°. Again ∠B = 90° - θ = 90° - 25° = 65°. Therefore the possible measures of ∠B are 50° or 65°.

method.method_draft: Use a circumcenter/inscribed-angle route. Read from the figure that A, B, C are on the large triangle, P is connected to C and reflected to Q across AC, forming triangle PCQ beside side AC. From the text, since P is the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC, P is the circumcenter of triangle ABC, so PA = PB = PC and A, B, C lie on the circle centered at P. Therefore ∠ABC is an inscribed angle subtending chord AC, while ∠APC is the corresponding central angle, so ∠ABC = 1/2∠APC. Next use the reflection across AC: A and C stay fixed, so AP = AQ and CP = CQ; combined with AP = PC, quadrilateral A-P-C-Q has all four sides equal, or at least triangle PCQ is isosceles with CP = CQ and AC bisects the angle at C. Let γ = ∠PCQ. In triangle APC, because AP = PC and AC bisects the reflected configuration, ∠APC = 180° - γ. In triangle PCQ, either the 50° angle is one of the equal base angles, giving γ = 80°, or the 50° angle is the vertex angle at C, giving γ = 50°. Hence ∠B = 1/2(180° - γ), giving 50° in the first case and 65° in the second case.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, point $P$ is the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of $AB$ and $BC$, and point $Q$ is symmetric to point $P$ with respect to $AC$. Connect $PC$, $PQ$, and $CQ$. If in $\triangle PCQ$ there is an angle of $50^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle B$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect AP and BP as shown in the diagram: \\
$\because$ Point P is the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC,\\
$\therefore$ PA = PB = PC,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$PAB = $\angle$PBA, $\angle$PBC = $\angle$PCB, $\angle$PAC = $\angle$PCA,\\
$\because$ Point Q is symmetric to point P with respect to AC,\\
$\therefore$ PC = QC, $\angle$PCA = $\angle$QCA,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$CPQ = $\angle$CQP,\\
(1) When $\angle$CPQ = $\angle$CQP = 50$^\circ$, $\angle$PCQ = 80$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$PCA = 40$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$PAC = 40$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$PAB + $\angle$PBA + $\angle$PBC + $\angle$PCB = 180$^\circ$ - $\angle$PAC - $\angle$PCA = 100$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ 2$\angle$ABP + 2$\angle$PBC = 100$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ABP + $\angle$PBC = 50$^\circ$, i.e., $\angle$ABC = 50$^\circ$,\\
(2) When $\angle$PCQ = 50$^\circ$, $\angle$PCA = 25$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$PAC = 25$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$PAB + $\angle$PBA + $\angle$PBC + $\angle$PCB = 180$^\circ$ - $\angle$PAC - $\angle$PCA = 130$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ 2$\angle$ABP + 2$\angle$PBC = 130$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ABP + $\angle$PBC = 65$^\circ$, i.e., $\angle$ABC = 65$^\circ$,\\
In conclusion, $\angle$ABC is \boxed{50^\circ} or \boxed{65^\circ}

Let ∠ABP = ∠PAB = x and ∠PBC = ∠PCB = y. Then the angles of triangle ABC are x + θ, x + y, and y + θ, so 2x + 2y + 2θ = 180°. Therefore x + y = 90° - θ. Hence ∠B = 90° - 40° = 50°. Case 2: If the 50° angle is the vertex angle ∠PCQ, then 2θ = 50°, so θ = 25°. Again ∠B = 90° - θ = 90° - 25° = 65°. Therefore the possible measures of ∠B are 50° or 65°.
